explanations.Explain how an aborted command request i: An aborted command request is distinguished at three points in frontend/src/services/api.ts: signal?.throwIfAborted() runs before the fetch, so a pre-aborted signal rejects with exactly the caller's signal.reason (the test compares identity with rejects.toBe(alreadyAborted.signal.reason)); the fetch init forwards the signal only when supplied (`...(signal === undefined ? {} : { signal })`); and the catch clause rethrows the rejection itself when signal?.aborted or when the error is an object whose name is 'AbortError' (a DOMException or a fetcher-thrown Error with that name), while any other rejection keeps the pre-existing Network('Cannot reach the server. Check your connection and try again.'). The frozen base's bare `catch { throw new Network(...) }` relabelled every cancellation as a transport failure; the named case 'forwards an aborted command request as a cancellation rather than a network failure' covers both aborted paths by identity and both transport-failure paths (undefined signal and a fresh non-aborted signal) expecting Network with the existing message, so a subtle mis-merge fails it. Refusal decoding and every existing caller keep their behaviour because the only new failure on the success path is `response.ok && document._tag === 'None'`: the opaqueredirect/302/303 -> Unauthenticated check, refusal(response.status, payload) building MutationRefused from exactly the server's members (code, message, optional current_version, current_revision, allowed_actions, details), and the non-JSON status path (409 -> Conflict, 403 -> Forbidden for commands, Unauthenticated for 401) are byte-for-byte the base logic, and `signal?: AbortSignal` is a trailing optional parameter on postPortalCommand and postGoalCommand so frontend/src/features/attention/attention.tsx (4-argument call) and frontend/src/features/goals/detail.tsx (4-argument calls) compile and run unchanged without it. Executed evidence: frontend-typecheck, frontend-lint, the full 238-test frontend suite and the 26-case browser baseline all passed on the sealed revision, and the third named case pins the unchanged JSON payloads, request init (CSRF header, cache: 'no-store', redirect: 'manual') and refusal/status mapping.
explanations.Explain why a 2xx command body the decod: frontend/src/services/api.ts postPortalCommand decodes the body with Schema.decodeUnknownOption(Schema.parseJson(Schema.Unknown))(await response.text()); when the result is None (HTML or other non-JSON text, truncated JSON, whitespace-only, or an empty 204 body) the pre-change code still returned `payload`, which is null — a receipt-shaped success for a body that carries no receipt, so a caller could announce acceptance it never verifiably received. Resolving must reject instead because the outcome the UI reports is derived from this return value: frontend/src/features/goals/detail.tsx registers `postGoalCommand` as the `command` useMutation and its onSuccess announces `${actionLabel(...)} accepted by the server.` plus query invalidations, and frontend/src/features/attention/attention.tsx NewGoalButton calls `postPortalCommand` for goal creation and its onSuccess announces 'The server created the Goal.' — that is the caller path that would otherwise announce an accepted command from a placeholder. The change makes response.ok with document._tag === 'None' throw UnexpectedResponse{message: 'The server response could not be read safely. Refresh or contact your operator.', status: response.status, transient: false}, so those callers run their onError branch, and readRetry(0, failure) is false so an unverifiable command is not silently auto-retried. Executed evidence: the named case 'rejects an unreadable command success body instead of returning a placeholder receipt' asserts instanceof UnexpectedResponse, the exact response status and transient:false for four bodies (HTML text, '{"receipt":' truncation, whitespace, null/204) across both postPortalCommand and postGoalCommand, and asserts readRetry is false; stored vitest-report.json records it passed exactly once at module level (focused-tests exit 0); reverting the api.ts hunk makes it fail by resolving null.

Receipt-truth fix verified in frontend/src/services/api.ts postPortalCommand: when response.ok and `Schema.decodeUnknownOption(Schema.parseJson(Schema.Unknown))(await response.text())` yields None (non-JSON text, truncated JSON, empty 204), it now throws UnexpectedResponse{message: 'The server response could not be read safely. Refresh or contact your operator.', status: response.status, transient: false} instead of resolving the null placeholder; readRetry(0, err) is false so the command is never auto-retried. Reverting only those lines makes the named case fail (it resolves null). Executed evidence: checks/attempt-0001/focused-tests/vitest-report.json lists 'rejects an unreadable command success body instead of returning a placeholder receipt' exactly once, module-level, status passed; gate exit 0; my independent rerun of the coordinator's recompute_gate/inspect_attempt over the stored evidence revalidates every gate (subject_hash_before/after == sealed for all 11).

Abort handling verified in frontend/src/services/api.ts: postPortalCommand calls signal?.throwIfAborted() before fetch, forwards the signal only when defined (`...(signal === undefined ? {} : { signal })`), and in catch rethrows when `signal?.aborted` or the rejection's name is 'AbortError'; otherwise it throws the unchanged Network('Cannot reach the server. Check your connection and try again.'). The named case 'forwards an aborted command request as a cancellation rather than a network failure' asserts rejection identity (`rejects.toBe(signal.reason)` for a pre-aborted controller; `rejects.toBe(abortError)` for an abort during flight and for two AbortError-shaped fetcher rejections with no signal passed) and asserts TypeError transport failures still reject as Network with the existing message for undefined and fresh non-aborted signals. The frozen base's catch-all `throw new Network(...)` relabelled every abort, so the test fails on it.

Preserved behaviour verified by the named case 'keeps a JSON command body its decoded payload and a refusal its own status error' and by the diff shape: 2xx JSON bodies (object with extra members, array, string, number, false, null) resolve exactly the decoded payload; request init keeps method POST, credentials same-origin, Accept/content-type/x-csrf-token headers, JSON body, cache no-store, redirect manual; non-2xx JSON refusals still become MutationRefused carrying the server's code/message and optional current_version/current_revision/allowed_actions/details; non-JSON 409/403 still map to Conflict/Forbidden and 302/303/401 to Unauthenticated (redirect check unchanged and ordered before decoding). That case is a preservation guard (it would also pass on the frozen base) — its role, per the frozen outcome, is to pin 'keeps resolving exactly the payload it decodes today'. The read path (request/decodeBody), readRetry and the refusal helpers are untouched by the diff; frontend suite 238/238 tests and browser baseline 26/26 passed on the sealed revision.

Named-test evidence is executed, not fabricated: the derived run stored in checks/attempt-0001/focused-tests/result.json (vitest_argv: vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile <gate-dir>/vitest-report.json src/services/command-receipts.test.ts, exit 0, stdout 'JSON report written to ...') produced a report where each of the three frozen full names appears exactly once with status 'passed' and empty ancestorTitles (module level), numFailedTests 0, numPendingTests 0. frontend/src/services/command-receipts.test.ts imports only vitest, ./api and ./commands, performs no filesystem writes, and asserts against the real postPortalCommand/postGoalCommand with fetcher mocks only at the HTTP boundary, so the report cannot be produced by the test file; the reporter overwrites any earlier content at the end of its own run. No required test was removed, skipped or weakened (new file has no describe/skip/todo; api.test.ts and api.fixtures.ts are unchanged).

browser-acceptance (gate exit 0) executed only the repository baseline specs browser/tests/workspace-shell.spec.mjs and browser/tests/portal-execution-control.spec.mjs at desktop and mobile chromium (26/26 passed, stored stdout); it asserts no command-receipt or abort behaviour of the changed functions. The new decoder/abort behaviour is therefore evidenced by the focused unit test alone, which exercises the real production functions through per-test fetcher mocks at the HTTP boundary. The frozen task states no rendered or accessibility claim, so no browser assertion of this behaviour was required; recorded so acceptance evidence is not over-claimed.

Boundary, not a defect: postPortalCommand decodes with `await response.text()` (pre-existing) rather than the read path's fatal TextDecoder (decodeBody), so a 2xx body with invalid UTF-8 bytes whose U+FFFD-substituted text still parses as JSON resolves a payload instead of rejecting. The frozen outcome defines the reject condition as a body the existing decoder cannot read (document._tag === 'None') and requires JSON bodies to keep resolving exactly the payload decoded today, so the implementation matches the contract; noted as the limit of the 'unreadable' definition for anyone reading it as byte-level validation.
